about: Строки таблиц расхода Aircraft Commerce (выпуски 59–142, 2008–2022), извлечены 17.10.2026 из PDF издателя как текст и глазами по печатным страницам не сверены. Нужны для сверки модели расхода openap (fca burn --calib, решение 225). Числа — как напечатаны; единицы — в именах полей.

rows.document: Aircraft Commerce Issue No. 142 (Jun/Jul 2022), 'A220-100/-300 fuel burn & operating performance'
rows.quote: City-pair: ORD-DTW, Aircraft variant: E-190, Engine variant: CF34-10E6, Seats: 100, Payload carried - lbs: 19635, ESAD - nm: 200, Flight time - mins: 45, Trip fuel - USG: 468, USG per seat: 4.68, Diff USG: 1.18, % diff: 33.6%, Trip fuel/ USG ASM: 0.021
rows.notes: Fuel column printed 'Trip fuel - USG' under table title 'BLOCK FUEL PERFORMANCE OF ...'; article prose never defines block vs trip. Methodology: CAE Flight Plan Manager, IFR, min-range-cruise Mach, 52 weeks of flight plans (average winds), taxi-out 15 min / taxi-in 8 min ('this would affect total fuel carried'), 5% reserve fuel policy, fuel to alternate carried, no diversions/delays, 85% passenger load factor, 231 lb per passenger incl. baggage, fuel density 6.7 lb/USG. Time column is 'Flight time - mins' (not block time), so fuel is most likely trip (airborne) fuel, but this is not stated explicitly. Payload printed = passengers carried (85% LF, from spec table) x 231 lb; 'Seats' column = dual-class configuration seats; 'USG per seat' = fuel / seats. Table source: CAE Flight Plan Manager. Route table prints ESAD ranges ORD-ATL 543-551 and ORD-PHL 547-548, which do not exactly match the per-row values of the 737/A319/A220-300 table (ATL 543-545, PHL 548-551) - possible print/extraction swap. pax and OEW/DOW (lb) taken from the article's spec table. Spec table lists engine CF34-10E5 for E-190LR; fuel table row prints CF34-10E6.

Column printed 'Trip fuel burn (USG)', but text: 'A taxi time of 20 minutes has been factored into the fuel burns' and fuel 'only includes the fuel used for the trip and taxiing' -> trip + taxi.
